Codex s-pck-2c-host, 2026-10-08, source audit at 492d118b1: STOP under the lane's missing-ACL2-entry rule, before step 1. No host/book changes or deletions. The accepted seam still lacks a concrete open selection: books/paged-checkpoint-host.lisp:115-137 calls pgs-open on the model DISK, then fn-pck-capture-of-pages on all pages and FILE to obtain S. DISK is the list representation (books/pagestore.lisp:323-340), FILE is the payload octet list. No alternate fn-pck-open-selection caller/refinement entry exists in books/ or host/. Passing those inputs would rematerialize the whole store, including payloads. Proposed statement for S audit: an entry over the verified resident-open verdict, checkpoint S, total count, K and retained log start returns the same selection as fn-pck-open-selection under named open-correspondence and count/start equations. The host must not reproduce the comparisons. This is a new seam contract, not a discharged premise or an implemented function.

Codex s-pck-2c-host: concrete recovery summary is missing. fn-pck-root-tree-of-capture (paged-checkpoint.lisp:322) persists four fold roots, F and PLEN. fn-pck-x-open (paged-checkpoint-open.lisp:228-256) returns only those four roots, rows, reads and stobjs; line 252 drops fields 4 and 5. Its capture keystone (line 1963) likewise covers only four roots. fn-pck-f-of-pages (:876) is a logical page-list decoder, not a pgs-mem entry. fnn-recover-log (host/native/io.lisp:9003, especially :9026-9032) needs F before choosing journal segments. The next publish also needs committed PLEN rather than physical EOF: an interrupted payload append can leave bytes beyond the selected root. Proposed statement for S audit: a guard-verified resident root decoder returns F and PLEN equal to fields 4/5 of the encoded root, with the same resident-image premise as the open; extend the open result or expose that decoder. Preserve the existing capture theorem and add the summary theorem. Do not invent host decoding or derive the committed boundary from EOF.

Codex s-pck-2c-host: A2's no-octet-list premise does not match fn-cpl-write-frames (checkpoint-payloads.lisp:794): PS is a list of payload octet lists, consumed by fn-cpl-write-frame (:787), whose implementation appends P. It is not an arena/buffer range input. fn-pck-x-encode-row (paged-checkpoint-exec.lisp:228) and fn-pck-x-tl (paged-checkpoint-stage.lisp:67) also materialize via fn-row-wire-of. Proposed statement for S audit: an arena/range frame writer, with concrete extent length and digest outputs, refines fn-cpl-write-frame for the denoted payload and establishes the staging trailer/ref equations. In addition, fn-cpl-payloadp (checkpoint-payload-ref.lisp:97) requires 1+LEN < 2^64, stronger than the seam's LEN < 2^64; the caller must discharge the actual bound. No host-side payload/frame implementation added.

Codex s-pck-2c-host: guard verification remains necessary before declaring native entries. fn-pck-publish-plan-at, fn-pck-open-selection, fn-pck-x-stage-rows and fn-pck-x-stage-root explicitly use :verify-guards nil, with no later verify-guards events for them anywhere in books/. fn-pck-x-open does have verify-guards at paged-checkpoint-open.lisp:409. Certification of a logic-mode book does not establish :common-lisp-compliant for these entries; books/definterface.lisp:14-43 checks that class against the world. Do not declare the missing class or bypass dispatch. S must audit actual caller guards together with the proposed concrete contracts before proof work.
